name: Assistant screen context
plain: Lets the assistant see what is on screen to answer questions.
meaning: The system can capture the screen, or a camera view, and hand it to an assistant. Apps can opt out of capture on Android and iOS.

android.prompt_ui: Default assistant selection; Circle to Search gesture
android.revocation: Settings > Apps > Default apps > Digital assistant
android.note: Android 15 adds assist content structure to AssistContent; Circle to Search is Google owned.

ios.permission: None; NSUserActivity and App Intents expose content
ios.prompt_ui: Visual Intelligence (camera control) iPhone 16; onscreen awareness in iOS 26
ios.api_surface: App Intents entities, Visual Intelligence search integration (iOS 26)
ios.note: Screenshots can be shared with ChatGPT after consent.

limits.headline: Can see your screen when you call the assistant, if it is your chosen one
limits.user_action: You set an assistant as default, or use Circle to Search or Visual Intelligence
can: Look at the screen content to answer a question about it
Share a screenshot with ChatGPT on iPhone after you agree
Use camera based search on iPhone 16 and newer
cannot: Look at your screen when you have not called the assistant
Be used by any app that is not the default assistant on Android
Share a screenshot with ChatGPT on iPhone without your consent
limits.reach_label: Only when you ask the assistant
limits.differs: Android lets your chosen default assistant see the screen, and Circle to Search is Google's. iPhone uses Visual Intelligence from iOS 18.2.

story.what_it_is: Lets an assistant see what is on the screen so it can answer questions about it.

marketing.name: Visual Intelligence
marketing.pitch: Apple pitches Visual Intelligence as a way to learn about what you see with the camera or on screen.

marketing.name: Circle to Search
marketing.pitch: Google pitches Circle to Search as a way to search anything on screen with a gesture.

story.for_you: You circle a pair of shoes in a video or point the camera at a plant, and the assistant tells you what it is. It sees whatever is on screen at that moment.
story.for_makers: Makers of assistants get rich context without apps adding anything. It is great for search and help, but it can capture private things on screen.

use_cases.example: You circle a jacket in a video and see where to buy it.
You point at a math problem and get a step by step hint.
You point your camera at a sign and get a translation.
The assistant reads what is on screen aloud.
You ask what a meme in a chat means.
You ask the assistant for a tip about a puzzle on screen.
A bank app can block screen capture on sensitive pages.

story.android_note: Circle to Search is a Google feature. Apps get assist data from Android 15.
story.ios_note: Visual Intelligence needs iPhone 16. iOS 26 adds on screen awareness.

history.change: Launched on Pixel 8 and Galaxy S24
